S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.

subtypes.Future Hopelessness: The persistent conviction that the future holds no possibility of improvement.
subtypes.Belief in Impossibility of Improvement: The belief that the current situation will absolutely not get better.
subtypes.Helpless Resignation: A state of helplessness and resignation, believing that nothing will change despite effort.
subtypes.Chronic Pessimism: A persistent tendency to view everything negatively and fail to consider positive possibilities.

symptom.disease_info: Persistent Depressive Disorder (dysthymia) is characterized by a chronically low mood lasting at least two years in adults, with only brief periods of remission. Individuals often function day to day but at a reduced level, experiencing the depression as part of their usual personality or life, which can delay recognition and treatment. Compared with major depressive disorder, the symptoms are typically less acute but more enduring, leading to long-term interpersonal, occupational, and quality-of-life impairment. It frequently coexists with other psychiatric conditions and may be punctuated by superimposed major depressive episodes ("double depression").

patient.stressor: Johnathan traces the beginning of his prolonged low stretch to the period surrounding his divorce a little over three years ago, when his long hours on municipal contracts and weekend side jobs had been straining the marriage for years. After the separation, he poured himself even more into work and community projects, taking every landscaping contract he could and volunteering at the community garden to avoid being alone in his small apartment. Over time, he noticed that activities that used to restore him—weekend hikes above Aguadilla, cooking elaborate family meals, leading bomba dances—felt more like obligations he was going through out of habit, and he started turning down invitations from relatives, including Sunday dinners with his parents. It was only when his sister commented that he seemed like he was "just existing" and his crew started pointing out his increasing rigidity with schedules and lack of interest in new designs that he agreed to see a doctor at a local clinic, who then referred him for a psychiatric evaluation.
patient.chief_complaint: I’ve felt this low, empty mood hanging over me for years now, like I can’t shake feeling down no matter what I do.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days it feels like there’s this gray cloud sitting on my chest, like even when I’m out on a beautiful property or at the community garden, I’m just going through the motions and feel kind of hollow inside instead of enjoying anything.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: By the time I finish a regular workday, I’m wiped out in a way that doesn’t make sense for me—I sit down on the couch and feel too drained to cook a proper meal or even wash the dishes, no matter how much I rest.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.
S083.manifestation: I catch myself thinking, ‘This is just how my life is now,’ like the joy and family stuff I used to have is gone for good and there’s no real point planning for anything better because it never seems to actually change.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: Because I’m always feeling low and worn down, I’ve started turning down extra landscaping jobs, backing out of family dinners, and letting basic things like cooking and keeping my place tidy slide, which has my sister and crew worrying that I’m not really taking care of myself or my responsibilities anymore.
add_requirements.duration: I can trace this heavy, low mood and sense of just going through the motions back to around the time of my divorce a little over three years ago, and it really hasn’t let up since then.
